description: Find the smallest possible last value of a strictly increasing positive array of length n whose bitwise AND is x.
intuition: Every value must contain all set bits of x. Put the bits of n − 1 into the zero-bit positions of x. BigInt avoids JavaScript’s 32-bit bitwise truncation.
approach: Every value must contain all set bits of x. Put the bits of n − 1 into the zero-bit positions of x. BigInt avoids JavaScript’s 32-bit bitwise truncation.
explanation: Every value must contain all set bits of x. Put the bits of n − 1 into the zero-bit positions of x. BigInt avoids JavaScript’s 32-bit bitwise truncation.

timeComplexityBreakdown.variables: B = bitLength(x) + bitLength(n − 1), using unit-cost integer operations.

phases.label: Convert values and initialize the bit mask
Scan set bits of x and fill zero positions with bits of n − 1

timeComplexityBreakdown.note: Each iteration advances the mask by one bit. There are at most bitLength(x) occupied positions to skip plus bitLength(n − 1) positions to fill. The problem bounds keep values within a small fixed number of bits; unbounded arbitrary-precision bit costs are outside this unit-cost model.

complexityVariables.n: Required number of elements in the increasing array.
complexityVariables.x: Required bitwise AND of all elements in the array.
complexityVariables.B: Sum of the bit lengths of x and n − 1.
